subtopics.title: Equation of a straight line
subtopics.exposition: The standard form of a straight line equation is y = mx + c, where m is the gradient and c is the y-intercept. The gradient between two points is m = (y2 − y1)/(x2 − x1), which is equal to (y1 − y2)/(x1 − x2). The equation of a straight line through two points comes from the general formula (y − y1)/(x − x1) = (y2 − y1)/(x2 − x1), where (x, y) is any point on the line. The general line formula can also be written as y − y1 = m(x − x1). To find the equation of a straight line through two given points, write down the general formula (y − y1)/(x − x1) = (y2 − y1)/(x2 − x1), then substitute the coordinates and simplify to make y the subject. When finding the equation of a line through two given points, label one point's coordinates (x1, y1) and the other's (x2, y2).

subtopics.title: Parallel and perpendicular lines
subtopics.exposition: A line that runs parallel to the x-axis is called a horizontal line and has a gradient of zero. A line that runs parallel to the y-axis is called a vertical line and its gradient is undefined. Two parallel lines are always the same distance apart and have equal gradients. If two lines intersect perpendicularly, the product of their gradients is equal to −1. If line WX is perpendicular to line YZ, then mWX × mYZ = −1. Perpendicular lines have gradients that are the negative inverses of each other. A horizontal line's gradient is zero because there is no vertical change: m = (change in y)/(change in x) = 0/(change in x) = 0. A vertical line's gradient is undefined because there is no horizontal change: m = (change in y)/(change in x) = (change in y)/0 = undefined. To compare gradients when one line is given as an equation, rearrange it into standard form y = mx + c to read off its gradient. Two lines are shown to be parallel by finding that the gradient calculated for one equals the gradient calculated for the other. To find an unknown coordinate using perpendicularity, write the relationship mAB × mCD = −1 with the gradients expressed from the given coordinates, then solve for the unknown.

subtopics.title: Points on a line
subtopics.exposition: A straight line is a set of points with a constant gradient between any two of the points. If two points lie on the same line, the two points are said to be collinear. For points A, B and C on the same straight line, the gradient is the same between any pair of them: mAB = mBC = mAC. To prove three points are on a straight line using the distance formula, calculate the distance between each pair of points and prove that the sum of the two smaller distances equals the longest distance. To test collinearity by the gradient method, calculate the gradient between two different pairs chosen from the three points. If the gradients calculated between the different pairs of points are equal (mAB = mBC = mAC), the points are on a straight line. To test collinearity by the distance method, calculate the three distances between each pair of the three points. If the sum of the two shorter distances between three points equals the longest distance, the points lie on the same straight line. There are two methods to prove that points lie on the same line: the gradient method and a method using the distance formula.
